items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: You know Sadie that used to play around here?

ctx.x: Earl Lumpfords, trombone, clarinet. Little fella, I can't think of his last name. His name was Manny. That's all I can think of. What did you mention? Banjo player. He was a kid too, by the way. We had to get permission from his father to take him along with us. And what happened over there? Well, we stayed there for quite a while and I think it got a little tough. Buddy Petit came back to New Orleans, Earl Lumpfords came back. So we got another trumpet player by the name of her, Mac Thomas, to play trumpet. And…
Was she related to Sadie? You know Sadie that used to play around here? She might have come after you left. Sadie Goodson, Clarice Goodson. She's a New York man, but you might have known.

items.title: Sadie Goodson Interview, 1984-12-12
items.q: And then the, uh, the tall, lanky clarinet player. You know him? No, I don't remember him. His name was Hall.

ctx.x: Alright, well we all know now.

Okay Sadie, what's today's date? Today is December, it's 11th, 1984. 1984, okay. Let me see now. I had a photograph I wanted to show you. You know any of those guys? I'm pretty. I played with his band. Yeah, do you know the drummer here? That's Chani? No, that's not Chani and him. That's Faso. Faso, uh. I don't know if you ever knew Faso. I don't think I knew him, no. That's George Washington. You may never have known him. He's from Uptown. No, I never knew him. That fella with the cap on and the cornet, you knew…
Okay. I think we should check and make sure that we are getting this okay before we go further, don't we?
